observations: Two black plastic power banks lying on a concrete floor.
The top power bank has a yellowish piece of paper or tape covering the front surface.
The bottom power bank has a visible black sticker on the front.
Both units have charging cables attached: one green and one blue.
The power banks appear to be used, with some surface wear and scuffs visible.
No brand names, logos, or model numbers are legible on the devices.

claims.evidence: The items are used and appear to be non-functional.
The front of the top unit is covered by tape, and the bottom unit has a sticker.
No specification plate or test results are visible.
The physical condition shows wear, but internal repair status cannot be confirmed remotely.

risks.risk: The batteries may be dead or unable to hold a charge.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading the battery voltage or a video of the power banks charging and powering a device.

risks.risk: The capacity (mAh) is unknown, which is the primary factor in determining value.
risks.proof: A photo of the specification sticker on the back of the power bank.

risks.risk: The internal circuitry may be damaged or faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the power banks successfully charging a phone or powering a device.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the specification sticker on the back of the power banks.
Video of one of the power banks charging a phone or powering a device.
Photo of the charging cables to check for damage.
response.reason: The items are clearly used power banks. While they appear to be non-functional, they can be priced at their worst-case value as scrap units.
